Summary.Name: DeepCORO-JEPA
Summary.Description: One EchoJEPA video encoder (ViT-L) that segments the coronary tree into 26 SYNTAX classes itself and, from up to 12 diagnostic coronary angiography runs per study, predicts for each of 18 coronary segments the % diameter stenosis, the probability of a significant lesion and the probabilities of calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (CTO), plus LAD-territory FFR and iFR (value and probability of an abnormal result). Each probability comes with a yes/no call at a threshold chosen on the validation set. The encoder runs at most twice per study: full views at 224 px, then up to 4 tracked 320 px crops per segment. No segmentation map has to be provided. Version 1.1.0 serves model v13. Earlier working name: DeepCORO-Integrated.
Summary.Training_run: Weights & Biases run 400d0a77 of project mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation: https://wandb.ai/mhi_ai/deepcoro-segmentation/runs/400d0a77

Mechanism.Outcome: Per-segment coronary stenosis, calcification, thrombus and chronic total occlusion (18 segments) and LAD FFR/iFR
Mechanism.Output: segments.<segment>.stenosis_pct (0-100), .prob_significant (label: >= 70%, left main >= 50%), .prob_threshold, .significant (true when prob_significant > prob_threshold), .calcif_prob, .calcif, .thrombus_prob, .thrombus, .cto_prob, .cto (each flag true when its probability > the threshold of that finding); lesion_thresholds.operating_point, .calcif, .thrombus, .cto; lad_physiology.ffr, .ifr, .ffr_abnormal_prob (FFR <= 0.80), .ifr_abnormal_prob (iFR <= 0.89), .ffr_abnormal_threshold, .ifr_abnormal_threshold, .ffr_abnormal, .ifr_abnormal, .operating_point; n_videos, encoder_passes
Mechanism.Target_population: Adults undergoing diagnostic coronary angiography at MHI
Mechanism.Input_data_source: Diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (multi-frame XA DICOM)
Mechanism.Model_type: Deep learning: EchoJEPA ViT-L video encoder with its own segmentation decoder, tracked segment crops and per-segment attention pooling; stenosis and lesion (calcification, thrombus, CTO) heads on each segment; LAD physiology head on the left main / LAD / diagonal features

Model.Purpose: Read stenosis severity and three lesion findings in every coronary segment and estimate LAD physiology from the angiogram alone
Model.Output: 18 stenosis percentages, probabilities and yes/no calls; 18 x 3 lesion probabilities and yes/no flags; LAD FFR/iFR values, abnormal probabilities and yes/no calls

Uses_and_directions.General_use: Research preview of segment-level stenosis and lesion reading and image-only LAD physiology estimation.
Uses_and_directions.Target_population_and_use_case: Adults with diagnostic coronary angiography. Upload the diagnostic left and right coronary contrast runs (no PCI, stent or ventriculography runs); up to 12 are used, chosen by SeriesTime.
Uses_and_directions.Before_using_this_model: Held-out test (3,194 studies / 2,941 patients): stenosis macro AUROC 0.885 (DeepCORO-CLIP 0.850, EchoJEPA 0.851); mean per-segment Pearson r 0.50, 9 of 18 segments above 0.5. LAD FFR/iFR pooled AUROC 0.69 (95% CI 0.63-0.75; 274 measurements), FFR alone 0.72, iFR alone 0.68. Lesion findings, area under the precision-recall curve averaged over segments: calcification 0.118, thrombus 0.304, CTO 0.133; these are not better than the reference models (best reference 0.125, 0.410 and 0.139). Confirm every reading on the images.

Warnings_and_limitations.Input_selection: The model was trained only on diagnostic left/right coronary contrast runs without stents. This version does not filter uploads; PCI, stent, ventriculography or non-contrast runs will degrade the output.
Warnings_and_limitations.Distal_and_branch_segments: Agreement with the cath report is weaker for the posterolateral branch, distal LAD, distal LCx, diagonals, marginals, ramus and posterior LV branch (r 0.20-0.48).
Warnings_and_limitations.Physiology: LAD FFR/iFR outputs reach AUROC 0.69 on test and do not replace invasive measurement; FFR alone was tested on only 76 measurements. The earlier model v12 (container version 1.0.0) reached 0.72 on the same test set; the difference is within its confidence interval (+0.029, 95% CI -0.014 to 0.075).
Warnings_and_limitations.Video_encoding: DICOMs are converted exactly as the training videos (MJPG AVI). About 13% of training/test videos had been stored as MP4; for those studies the DICOM path differs slightly from the AVI-based test results.
Warnings_and_limitations.Confidence_Scores: Probabilities are not calibrated. The yes/no calls use thresholds chosen on the internal validation set, not validated clinical operating points; a call is positive when probability > threshold. Stenosis and pressure use the threshold with the highest geometric mean of sensitivity and specificity. On the held-out test set: FFR <= 0.80 at 0.2644: sensitivity 0.83, specificity 0.49 (76 measurements); iFR <= 0.89 at 0.4337: sensitivity 0.59, specificity 0.70 (198 measurements); significant stenosis, mean of 18 segments: sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.80, positive predictive value 0.25, negative predictive value 0.98.
Warnings_and_limitations.Flags: Thresholds of rarely diseased segments are low (for example 0.02 for distal LCx), so a segment can be flagged with a low probability and a low estimated percentage. At least one segment is flagged for stenosis in 42% of test studies without any significant lesion in the report. FFR and iFR are separate outputs and their calls can disagree in the same study.
Warnings_and_limitations.Lesion_flags: Calcification, thrombus and CTO are rare (1.9%, 0.2% and 0.7% of segments in the test set), so their flags use one threshold per finding set for 99% specificity on the validation set. On the held-out test set (57,492 segment readings): calcification at 0.2225: sensitivity 0.19, specificity 0.990, positive predictive value 0.27; thrombus at 0.0851: sensitivity 0.51, specificity 0.992, positive predictive value 0.10; CTO at 0.1570: sensitivity 0.37, specificity 0.990, positive predictive value 0.21. Most findings are missed and most flags are false: an absent flag does not exclude the finding. Lesion labels come from the angiography report.

Changelogs.1.2.0: 2026-11-13: Same model (v13), weights and thresholds. The HTML report draws the 18 segments on a coronary schema instead of a table. An optional additionalMetadata.coronaryDominance (study majority of the angiogram procedure classifier over the diagnostic videos sent) is validated, returned as predictions.coronary_dominance, added to the diagnosis and used to draw the schema left or right dominant. In the report and diagnosis a CTO-flagged segment is shown as occluded at 100% (stenosis estimate kept in the JSON), thrombus flags are drawn as a filling defect, and the posterior LV branch is not shown (still in the JSON). For each flagged stenosis segment (up to 6) the report shows the tracked crop with the highest attention, the within-crop attention the model applied (recomputed exactly from the same forward call) and the full frame with the crop box; the JSON gets the matching metadata in predictions.explainability without images.
Changelogs.1.1.1: 2026-11-12: Same model (v13). Probabilities are returned with 6 decimals instead of 4 and every yes/no call is taken on the returned probability, so a response never shows a probability at its threshold next to a positive call.
Changelogs.1.1.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v13 (Weights & Biases run 400d0a77): adds calcification, thrombus and CTO probabilities and flags per segment and the Thresholds key lesion_operating_point. Stenosis is unchanged on test (macro AUROC 0.885 against 0.884); pressure AUROC is 0.69 against 0.72 for v12.
Changelogs.1.0.0: 2026-11-12: Serves model v12: 18-segment stenosis and LAD FFR/iFR with validation-derived thresholds.
